title: LENTICULAR
description: A full-width claim in Bricolage Grotesque ('Gentrit Rashiti builds web and phone apps for learners, care teams and shoppers.', with 'web' underlined in red) under a thin sticky lens bar holding one switch, Web [thumb] Phone, and the line 'Showing each product on the web.' Below, a wide lenticular print of Bayyinah TV on a bone ground: bayyinahtv.com cropped above the site's own marketing band, a thin band of App Store strips at its right edge; beside it the face labels (bayyinahtv.com ⇄ App Store), the fact that the same web app runs on the site and in both store apps, role and years, and three public links. Flip the switch or drag any print and the whole page turns: every print sweeps to its phone face, the underline moves to 'phone', and the index marks what runs on a phone.
signature: Type: Bricolage Grotesque 640 (opsz auto) for the claim at 66px (34px on a phone, four lines), with a size-adjusted local fallback measured on the claim; Public Sans for text; Gentrit Technical Mono 13px for years and the 16 → 2 line. Colour: bone ground #f7efea; ink #1f1518 sampled from bayyinahtv.com's ground; one accent #b41d02 sampled from its Start Learning button, job: the current face (switch thumb, active labels, the claim's underline, the index tags), focus and link hover; the prints carry all other colour; About sits on the ink. Motion: one driven value, the page lens angle (0 = web face, 1 = phone face; 0 → 9°). The switch's thumb drags 1:1 (22px = 9°), a tap springs (visualDuration 0.5 s, bounce 0.12), arrow keys jump; dragging any print drives the same angle and a release hands its velocity to spring.snap. Every print sweeps across its 4px lenses from the edge that turns away, all in step; each lens brings its own sheen (glints as seen flat on the first screen, glints at 9° and the lens seams on the second), and only the lenses whose cut moved are redrawn. Nothing plays at load. At rest each card shows a thin band of its second screen's strips at its right edge, so the material reads in a still.
rule: The page is one lenticular sheet: every picture holds two real screens of one product, and one lens angle for the whole page, set by the visitor, picks which screen every picture shows: the web or the phone.
designRead: Reading this as: a frontend and mobile developer for hiring managers and recruiters, leading with Bayyinah TV (one web app that runs on the website and inside both store apps), in a world of lenticular prints where every picture holds two real screens of one product.
hook: The site that is one lenticular sheet: flip Web to Phone, or drag any screenshot, and every product on the page turns from its website to its phone app, while the claim's underline moves from 'web' to 'phone'.
lead: Bayyinah TV: public and checkable (website, App Store, Google Play), 2023–26, frontend in the core team, and its key fact — the same web app runs on the site and inside both store apps — is exactly a two-face fact for a two-image print.
composition: first-screen.md #3, the claim drawn as a picture: one object holds the web page and the app listing. Masthead, then a sticky 48px lens bar (the Web/Phone switch and the live line), the claim full width, the print large on the left (8 of 12 columns), the project's facts, face labels and links in a narrow right column. Below: a reading block with bayyinah.org, rows that alternate print-left / two narrow phone prints / print-right on alternating grounds, a grouped index with platform tags, and About on the ink. Every section reads the one page angle.

fourAnswers.desktop: who: Gentrit Rashiti (claim and masthead) / what: web and phone apps (with 'web' underlined, and a Web/Phone switch right above) / for whom: learners, care teams and shoppers / proof: 'Frontend and mobile developer since 2021, now full stack. Based in Kosovo, working remotely.', bayyinahtv.com as a real screen at 38% of the first screen (no marketing numbers in view), Frontend core team 2023–26, links to the website, App Store and Google Play
fourAnswers.phone: who: Gentrit Rashiti / what: web and phone apps (claim in four lines, under the Web/Phone switch) / for whom: learners, care teams and shoppers / proof: the role and location line, the print (both faces cropped to the same 'Quran Studies Made Simple' headline), Frontend core team 2023–26, Website, App Store and Google Play links at the bottom edge of 844

allowed: C17: LCP on a shared machine at 4x ranged 0.72–1.14 s across production runs (0.81 / 0.97 s and 0.85 / 0.87 s in the final two); the hero is one 211 kB WebP at high priority and this page's own code is under 11 kB gzip
runs: production preview after the performance pass, --throttle 4, --interact "click:.lx-lensctl label:last-of-type" --interact-frames 60,150,300,600: PASS, 0 fails, 0 warnings; 1440 work 38%, CLS 0.008, LCP 0.82 s; 390 work 28%, CLS 0, LCP 0.78 s

production preview after the performance pass, --throttle 4, --interact "drag-right:.lx-hero .lx-card" --interact-frames 60,150,300,600: PASS, 0 fails, 0 warnings; CLS 0.008 / 0.004, LCP 0.76 / 0.76 s

holdback: Hooks 9: one value, driven continuously, visible in every section, carrying the web-and-phone fact, and after the performance pass it holds 60 fps at 4x CPU in headless with two prints in view (p95 16.8 ms; one 51 ms frame in 1 of 3 two-print runs at 1440). Original 8, not 9: the sheet is a real material idea, but the skeleton (claim over a screen, side column, rows, index, dark footer) is familiar. Actions and seniority 7: the page shows what was built, less of the judgment behind it. The static fallback is close to the canvas rest frame but not pixel-identical (glint and edge band are canvas-only; a 180 ms fade covers the swap); mid-turn, the seams now show only on the lenses that show the second screen.
skillNotes: Helped: (1) M3's test, 'explain the effect in one sentence of engineering', pushed me past a striped CSS overlay to a computed lens: interlaced strips, a 2× cylindrical lens per 4px, the angle from the eye to each lens (tilt plus the lens's offset) picks the strip, so the flip sweeps across the card; and the lamp's glints are a specular term per lens. (2) motion.md's build order (static end state, cause, one token, interruptible, reduced branch, measure, scrub) mapped one-to-one, and the frequency gate settled that keyboard activation jumps. (3) first-screen.md's phone rules (work above 500px, text ≥ 11px in the crop) led to separate phone crops where both faces show the same headline. (4) The checker caught real things: words past the fold (C02), phone targets, a hidden canvas below the fold (M08), the word 'codebase' (T10f). Unclear or wrong: (a) There is no way to capture an interaction-triggered signature moment mid-flight: --frames times from navigation, element screenshots wait for a stable box so they never catch a rotation, and Playwright's fake clock did not drive motion's springs in real proportion. I scrubbed by dragging to fixed angles; the skill should ship '--interact <selector> --frames-after 60,150,300' or document clip screenshots at fixed states. (b) M08 counts an opacity-0 overlay canvas as a 'section that starts invisible' even though the picture under it is visible; a lazily built overlay is not a fade-up. (c) C17 on the required dev server is dominated by the host app's lazy router (two Suspense levels) and the unbundled module graph: 1.6 s dev vs 0.82 s production at 4×; the brief asks for dev + throttle, so every draft will warn; suggest measuring against a production preview or reporting time from the draft's own first paint. (d) Hard rule 9 allows 'one authored figure may build once' while first-screen.md lists 'loader, intro' as costing credibility; it is unclear whether a settle-on-load of the hero work (readable from the first frame) counts as the authored figure or as an intro. I read it as allowed and gated it (reduced motion, late lens, prior touch). (e) 'The claim sets in 2–4 lines at 32–40px' collides with a 15-word claim in a wide grotesque at 358px (5 lines at 34px); say which gives way: words, size or face. (f) The rule 'original or hook ≤ 7 → go back to direct' conflicts with a fixed round of at most two polish passes; there is no step for a re-direct. (g) The checker changed format mid-round (T23 now needs 4+ matches; --list and checks.md appeared later). (h) The tintedGround signal reads body's background; a draft inside a shared shell must restyle body at runtime to get credit. Missing: Crafted-band guidance that the material must read in a still capture (reviewers judge captures first), and a note that a static fallback should match the canvas's rest frame pixel for pixel so the swap does not pop. Polish pass: the new snippets/mechanism.md spec (capture after 5px, velocity hand-off, radio group, still-capture line) mapped directly onto the reviewer's findings, and --interact made the mid-flight capture possible without my own scripts. The radio pattern collides with the checker's focus test (C11 reads the focused element's own outline, so a visually hidden input would warn); covering the label with an appearance:none input that draws the ring solves both and could be in the snippet. A flaky C12 on the dev server can come from other builders' edits regenerating the shared Tailwind CSS via HMR; the checker could ignore shifts that coincide with a stylesheet swap, or say to confirm C12 on a production build. To a 9: motion.md's 8-to-9 test (name the one value, list every section it changes) turned a card trick into a page idea in one step; listing the sections exposed the two that did not change (the index and About) and gave them a job. Gaps: (a) the checker's long-frame count includes its own in-page DETECT analysis (an instrumented copy put the 1.0–1.3 s long frame inside DETECT), so 'long frames' cannot be read as the page's; mark its own window or exclude it. (b) The shell sets html { scroll-behavior: smooth }, and the checker's scrollTo(0,0) + 400 ms then captures full pages mid-glide at 4x; any sticky element shows up in the wrong place. The checker could scroll with behavior: 'instant', or the snippet for sticky bars could say to switch smooth scroll off. (c) There is no checker interaction for 'drag a control by N px' (drag-right moves 40% of the element's width, which on a 52px track is 21px, nearly the whole travel), so the switch's mid-states were scrubbed with my own script; a drag-to-fraction action would let reviewers see them. (d) A page-wide driven value multiplies per-frame cost by the prints in view; motion.md could say outright that only visible instances render and give the frame budget per instance. Performance pass: in headless Chrome at 4x (software raster and compositing) the costs were not where I expected. (a) A canvas clip made of many thin rectangles costs far more than the blits it guards (10–15 ms vs 2 ms per canvas); a one-row mask stretched down with destination-out, then the other picture with destination-over, does the same in three bounded blits. (b) A rounded clip (overflow: hidden + border-radius) on an element that turns in 3D, or a CSS radius on the canvas, forces an offscreen pass every frame; cut the corners into the pixels and drop the clip once the picture is up. (c) Every extra canvas layer that is updated or stretched over a turning card costs a full perspective quad; bake static overlays into the pictures. (d) A state flip that toggles an attribute on the page root, and a dozen labels easing colour on main-thread transitions, made the one long frame of a drag; set the attribute on the elements that show it, defer what is out of view to idle. (e) motion's frame.render batches canvas draws with the transform it renders. A snippet on 'per-frame canvas work under a 3D transform' with these four rules would have saved most of the pass. (f) The checker has no drag-and-hold interaction that reports frame times during the hold; I measured with my own scripts (rAF deltas and long-animation-frame entries during a 4.5 s drag).
polish: Fact (owner 3): the hero's bayyinahtv.com face is cropped above the site's marketing band at both widths (no '500k learners / +20y / 2000h' or testimonials in the first screen); the print is now 2880×1350 wide with four App Store frames as the second face, and a comment in the data records why.
Fact (owner 1): Design System v2 index line kept exactly as the owner rewrote it; the index is now grouped by employer and Vianova appears only on its own group.
Fact (owner 2): care row now says each screen moves over only when its test passes on both apps 'and none is live yet'; nothing says care teams use new screens.

Fact: Bayyinah authorship now 'A core frontend team, Gentrit among them, rebuilt the second version from an empty project.'; Offday result now 'About 200 tests, including checks that each team sees only its own data.'; 'programme' → 'program'; 'codebase' already removed.

Clarity/phone: role and location line under the claim at every width ('Frontend and mobile developer since 2021, now full stack. Based in Kosovo, working remotely.'); claim shortened to 'Gentrit Rashiti builds web and phone apps for learners, care teams and shoppers.' (four lines at 390).

Clarity: index links (internal and external) are underlined at rest with a → or ↗, and the index is grouped (Vianova, Public products, Incentiv, AvahiTech, Own products) with one rule per group; footer note rewritten in plain words (no '4 pixels').

Caption decision: no 'Drag or tap' instruction. The skill's hook-line rule forbids instructions, and the affordance is not invisible: two labelled faces in a radio group (one underlined), a grab cursor, the once-only peek after load, and now the resting edge band all show the card turns. The caption states the fact instead: 'Two real screens in one print: the website and the App Store page.'
Phone prints: Read to Feed and Viva Fresh are cropped to the app screen inside each store frame (phoneScreens.ts boxes), not the store art; Read to Feed pairs My Books ⇄ Achievements ('Badges').

Mechanism (snippets/mechanism.md): the face labels are a native radio group (one Tab stop, arrow keys; keyboard changes are instant, pointer changes spring); drag captures after 5px; release hands the hand's velocity over the last ~100 ms to spring.snap, so a flick turns the card (tested: 60px flick right → 9°, left → 0°); rubber band at both ends; tap toggles; the print is a role=group with an accessible name.

Still capture (the material reads at rest): each card is computed as seen from a little to its left, so its right edge shows a thin band (≤ 120px or 12% of the card) of the second screen's strips; lens seams now show only while the card is turned; the glint stays.

Craft: eye distance 5200 → 8000px and a narrower switch window, so the second face rests at 9° (was 14°) and its small text is barely skewed; the hero no longer starts on the App Store face (the 'dark slab' before images arrive is gone: the card is a light sheet until its picture paints) and instead peeks once from the website and back.
Phone captions stack (labels, then provenance) so nothing rewraps after load.

Not done in this pass (bounded): the reviewer's fix 5 (give the care card a web-and-phone pair) — there is no phone capture of the care platform, so the care pair stays team ⇄ one patient; the reviewer's note that only the hero card is likely to be turned is answered only by the resting edge band on every card.

Checker after the pass (dev, --frames 150,400,900 --throttle 4 --interact click on the App Store label, frames 60/150/300/600): PASS, 0 fails, 0 warnings, C17 allowed. Production preview at 4×: PASS, 0 warnings, CLS 0, LCP 0.68–0.82 s. Two dev runs during the pass showed a transient C12 (0.04–0.13) during the checker's scroll walk; it never appeared on the production build or in my own throttled replays, and the timing matched other builders' edits regenerating the shared Tailwind stylesheet through Vite HMR.
toNine: One driven value for the whole page: the page lens angle (0 = every print's web face, 1 = its phone face; θ = angle × 9°). One spring in Draft.tsx; every print's renderer reads it; a face store outside React (useSyncExternalStore) updates labels, the claim and the index without re-rendering the page.

A sticky 48px lens bar under the masthead at every width: one switch, Web [thumb] Phone. Native radio group (one Tab stop, arrow keys and Enter jump), a draggable thumb that follows the finger 1:1 with rubber band past both ends, tap to flip, release hands its velocity to the spring. Plain labels, no instruction line. On phones the bar holds the switch alone; it sits at the top because the bottom belongs to the browser toolbar and would cover the links under each print.
Live line 'Showing each product on the web.' / 'Showing each product on a phone, where it has one.' with aria-live=polite (visually hidden under 480px, still announced).

Every section reads the angle: the claim's underline (web → phone), the hero (bayyinahtv.com ⇄ App Store), bayyinah.org (Desktop ⇄ Phone), care (Care team ⇄ One patient, captioned 'Web only, so its second face is one patient.'), Read to Feed and Viva Fresh (Store page ⇄ App), Offday (Website ⇄ Phone, 'The same web app fits a phone.'), the All work index (a plain platform tag per row, Web / Phone / Web, phone, marked when it matches the face), and About's underline.
Dragging or flicking any print drives the same page angle (capture after 5px, 120px = 9°, velocity hand-off); a tap on a print toggles the page; any print's own face labels flip the whole page.
Normalised sweep: each print sweeps across its own width from the edge that turns away, so small and large prints flip in step (before, small cards flipped far earlier than the hero).

Peek dropped: a page-wide peek animated five elements at load (M11); the visible switch teaches instead. Reduced motion: no spring anywhere; taps, labels and keys jump; a drag follows the hand and jumps to the nearest face on release.

Performance (first pass, before the bounded performance pass): only prints in view drew per frame; compositing was a mask row → clip runs, one 14-row glint/seam overlay, static CSS shadows, setup across frames. Drag at 4x headless then: p95 33–50 ms (hero), 67 ms (two prints), 1–5 long frames per run.

Layout stability: a size-adjusted local fallback for Bricolage (size-adjust 94.3% measured on the claim), print canvases hidden until their first frame then a 180 ms fade over the static ; CLS 0–0.004 at 390, 0.008 at 1440.

Reviewer fixes: every print card is role=group with a name (hero: 'Bayyinah TV, website and App Store faces'); All work row links are 34px targets on desktop (pointer: fine) with 4px row padding; 44px targets on touch.
In-page jumps are instant while the draft is open (the shell's smooth scroll glided 5000px past every print and left full-page captures mid-scroll with the lens bar over the hero).
Facts and owner rules unchanged: the Design System v2 line verbatim, care 'none is live yet', no product marketing numbers in the first screen, no he/his.

Performance pass (on top of 71c0cc7; target p95 ≤ 20 ms and no long frame ≥ 50 ms at 4x while dragging): (1) only lenses whose cut moved are drawn, as bands of three bounded blits (B, a one-row mask stretched down with destination-out, A behind with destination-over) instead of a clip of ~100 thin rects (10–15 ms vs 4.5 ms per canvas at 4x); (2) the sheen is printed into the two screens once at setup (A: glints seen flat; B: glints at 9° and the lens seams), so nothing but lens bands changes during a turn (a per-frame sheen canvas and three opacity-faded sheen layers were measured and rejected); (3) after the lens fades in, the turning card no longer clips: corners are cut into the screens' pixels and the plain pictures under the lens are clipped away with clip-path (still read by screen readers), which removes an offscreen compositing pass per frame; (4) one draw per print per frame in motion's render step; (5) only cards in view are restyled, cards within a quarter screen catch up before they show; (6) a short flip frame: face marks set on the two dozen elements that show them (not a root attribute), out-of-view marks and fallback stacking deferred to idle, the print labels change at once instead of easing, the thumb on its own layer, the lens bar not selectable; (7) setup split into smaller frames. Result, drag at 4x headless (before → after): 1440 hero p95 33–50 → 16.8 ms, frames over 20 ms 24% → 1%, no long frames; 1440 hero + second print p95 67 → 16.7–16.8 ms, 50% → 2–3%, long frames 3–5 per run → one 51 ms frame in 1 of 3 runs; 390 hero p95 17–33 → 16.7–16.8 ms, no long frames; 390 two prints p95 33–50 → 16.8 ms, no long frames in the final 3 runs (one 139 ms outlier in 1 of 10 runs across the last two builds); spring from a tap with two prints p95 50 → 16.8 ms. Look: rest frames differ from before by 0.01–0.06/255 on average (the edge band's B strips now show B's faint seams); mid-turn by 0.2–1.0/255 (seams only on lenses showing B; glints no longer slide, they moved under 2 px over the whole turn). WebGL (idea 5) measured in a bench and dropped: SwiftShader + readback gave p50 33 ms for two canvases.
